summary: The article outlines strategies for integrating technology and digital literacy in classrooms under local education policies adopted after September 2023. It covers curriculum rollout, teacher training, equitable device access, infrastructure upgrades, collaborative and adaptive learning, digital citizenship, project-based learning, gamification, and new digital proficiency assessments. Named local officials and experts are cited as advocates for each strategy.
one_line: Overview of local education policy strategies since late 2023 for technology integration and digital literacy in classrooms, from curricula to assessments.
key_facts: John T. Malcolm, Chairperson of the Digital Education Council as of October 2023, led local districts in mandating digital literacy in school curricula.
On November 12, 2023, local education boards began rolling out an updated curriculum integrating technology into various subjects, influenced by research from Dr. Sophia R. Huang.
Marcus Ellington, Head of the Local Teachers' Association, stated on December 5, 2023 that budget allocation for teacher workshops and training sessions has increased.
Julia Kensington, Education Equity Coordinator, emphasized on January 15, 2024 that schools must provide tablets or laptops to students without access at home.
Infrastructure initiatives launched since late 2023 include enhancing Wi-Fi, setting up smart classrooms, and creating tech support hubs.
As of February 2024, schools have been using Google Classroom and Microsoft Teams for group projects and online discussions, a strategy highlighted by Leslie Tam.
Alexei Petrov, director of Innovation in Education, showcased adaptive learning platforms on March 3, 2024 as support for differentiated instruction and personalized learning.
Laura L. Ito, an environmental scientist turned educator, advocated project-based learning using digital tools on real-world problems on April 7, 2024.
Gamification specialist Andy J. Robertson praised the policy's inclusion of leaderboards and achievement badges.
Starting in the 2024-2025 school year, standardized tests will include sections evaluating students' digital competencies.
Assessment coordinator Irene Thompson is leading groundwork to align assessments with skills from integrated technology education.
Digital citizenship education covers online safety, respect, and responsibility, driven by misinformation and cyberbullying concerns.
